decision: One transcript_allowed flag on the existing call_settings row, default false
why: Serve and the CLI already share that row. After the key exists, the row wins so a later env value does not overwrite fernruf settings transcript on.

decision: Drop words at the show, socket, database, get_call, and webhook boundaries. Keep them in memory until the summary is built.
why: The summary still needs what was said. The stored call and the monitor must not.

decision: The call window still opens when the transcript is off, with the line Transcript is off. When it is on, the existing transcribed notice stays.
why: The operator still needs the call state. The notice should not be a second disclaimer.

decision: Spoken logs follow the flag on the settings object for that call
why: A shared data/fernruf.sqlite must not override a test, and a settings change mid-call must not start writing words into a call that began with the switch off. Call start copies the saved switch onto the object.

decision: demo-call still writes transcript.json into the directory the operator named
why: That file is an explicit local artifact, not the call database or data/calls.

decision: The MCP token cannot flip the switch
why: Same rule as the allowlist and international calling. The host sets it with the CLI.

decision: Ran pytest offscreen, ruff, and a working-tree gitleaks scan
why: The switch changes what a call stores and shows, so the suite has to pass with the display off.
evidence: 886 passed, 3 skipped; privacy tests rechecked 6 passed; gitleaks no leaks
